name: Taco Bell Cantina, Linda Mar (Pacifica)
notes: Construction 1971.6–1972.3; Opened: spring 1972 (grand opening late Apr 1972) as an A&W franchise on Bud Wiechers' beachfront lot — approved just before Proposition 20 (1972) created the Coastal Commission; a restaurant like it could not be built there today; Taco Bell: A&W closed in 1985 and the building became a Taco Bell that year (Pacifica Tribune, Jul 31, 1985); Cantina: renovated for about two months and reopened Jul 13, 2019 as a Taco Bell Cantina serving alcohol; the walk-up take-out window and surfboard rack kept; new fireplace and lounge seating inside; Exterior: dark brown wood siding in the A&W years and today, deck over the beach — the 2019 remodel was mainly inside, so one model covers 1972 to today; Model: outline from OpenStreetMap (© OSM contributors, ODbL; building and deck); split between restaurant and deck, wall and roof heights, window, sign and fire-pit positions estimated from the (blurred) orthophoto and descriptions — no photograph was examined

name: San Francisco Main Library
notes: Construction 1992.8–1996.29; Opened: completed 1995, opened Apr 18, 1996 (construction start estimated), replacing the 1917 Main Library across Fulton St (now the Asian Art Museum); built on Marshall Square, part of the block of the old City Hall (1872–1906); Architects: Pei Cobb Freed & Partners (James Ingo Freed) with Simon Martin-Vegue Winkelstein Moris (Cathy Simon); Design: Beaux-Arts granite fronts toward the Civic Center (Fulton and Larkin Sts) and modern planar sides toward Hyde and Grove Sts; a central five-storey skylit atrium; seven storeys; Model: outline, overall height (46 m) and the atrium square from OpenStreetMap (© OSM contributors, ODbL); cornice height, the set-back modern upper block and window bays estimated from photographs
